hero.eyebrow: About — the person behind the machine
lead: I'm Monish Kamwal — a Computer Science co-op student at Memorial University of Newfoundland, and an AI developer who builds machine-learning systems end to end.

Most of my work has been in the public sector: government RAG chatbots, the MLOps behind a fleet-management platform, and the cloud infrastructure around them. My interest is less the model itself than everything around it — how data gets versioned, how a bad model gets stopped before it ships, and how infrastructure can be created for a load test and torn down afterward.
This site is one of those systems, built on my own time. I'm based in St. John's, Newfoundland.

entries.what: The end-to-end MLOps platform this site fronts, run for under $5/month.

items.heading: What it is
items.body: An end-to-end MLOps platform that classifies browser sketches in real time. A 422k-parameter PyTorch CNN (15 classes, macro-F1 0.916) runs as ONNX on AWS Lambda for under $5/month, with a quality-gated training pipeline, weekly drift monitoring, a retrain loop from user feedback, and monthly ephemeral-EKS load tests.

items.heading: My role
items.body: Designed and built the whole system: a 7-stage DVC pipeline with Pandera validation, a champion/challenger quality gate in MLflow, keyless AWS deploys over OIDC (no stored keys, least-privilege IAM), dual-Terraform infrastructure, and this front-end.

items.heading: Stack
items.body: PyTorch · ONNX · FastAPI · AWS (Lambda · EKS · S3 · ECR) · Terraform · Helm · Prometheus · Grafana · k6 · DVC · MLflow · Evidently · GitHub Actions · Next.js

entries.what: A physics-informed network that predicts the motion of a chaotic double pendulum.

card.title: Hamiltonian Neural Network for a double pendulum

items.heading: What it is
items.body: A Hamiltonian Neural Network, built with Prof. Afework Solomon, that predicts the motion of a double pendulum — a classically chaotic system — by learning its energy rather than its trajectory directly.

items.heading: What I did
items.body: Implemented and trained the model in PyTorch and NumPy, reducing the loss by over 76% across 900 epochs, and plotted the training curve in Matplotlib.

items.heading: Stack
items.body: PyTorch · NumPy · Matplotlib

card.title: OLS regression: CEO compensation and renewable-energy use

items.heading: What it is
items.body: A short econometric study testing whether executive compensation correlates with a firm's renewable-energy use.

items.heading: What I did
items.body: Collected data from 24 firms, cleaned it, and ran an ordinary-least-squares regression over 60 data points in Statsmodels and Pandas. The result: no meaningful correlation between executive pay and sustainability effort.
